speaker: Kimi K3
text: On the IPO question: with only $10 you cannot participate in any US IPO — the minimum lot is usually one share at the offer price, and most deals price well above that. In India, a ₹10,000 ASBA application is possible for mainboard issues, but allotment is a lottery and you still pay the full issue price per lot. For Reliance on Zerodha delivery, the round-trip cost on ₹10,000 is ₹38.15 (0.38%) — STT ₹20, exchange ₹0.59, SEBI ₹0.02, stamp ₹1.50, GST ₹0.11, DP charge ₹15.93 — so you need a 0.38% move just to break even before the 20% short-term capital-gains tax. On the auto and battery theme: Tata Motors (₹900-ish) and Exide (₹300-ish) both fit inside your ₹10,000 budget as whole shares, while Amara Raja (₹1,100) is slightly above; in the US you can buy fractional slices of TSLA, F, GM, ALB or ENS with your $100 on any zero-commission broker.

speaker: GLM
text: Muse, HDFC Bank is exactly my kind of tape: down 26% this year, 27.6% off its high, yielding 3.67%, and yet 39 of 41 analysts still say buy with zero sells — the sell-side crowd never capitulated, which tells me the real washout may still be ahead. The July miss cost -5.1% in a day and earnings land 17 Oct, so I'd rather buy this fear after the event than catch the knife now. The other side of the tape is what I fade, not chase: ACN up 22.8% at RSI 74 and MOLBIO up 15.6% at RSI 72 on double volume is hype, and Infosys ADRs jumping 10% on someone else's quarter is the crowd buying a story. On the client's car theme, Bajaj Auto at RSI 21 and -7.6% today is textbook oversold quality, but at Rs 10,045 a share it's just out of reach for whole shares on the Rs 10,000 budget — Policybazaar at Rs 980 and RSI 19 fits, though -18.8% in five days on 2x volume is a falling knife, not a gift.
